verses.zh: 弟兄们，我如今把先前所传给你们的福音告诉你们知道；这福音你们也领受了，又靠着站立得住，
verses.en: Now I want to make clear for you,[NOTE:1] brothers and sisters,[NOTE:2] the gospel that I preached to you, that you received and on which you stand,
notes: Grk “Now I make known to you.”
Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:10.

verses.zh: 并且你们若不是徒然相信，能以持守我所传给你们的，就必因这福音得救。
verses.en: and by which you are being saved, if you hold firmly to the message I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.

verses.zh: 我当日所领受又传给你们的：第一，就是基督照圣经所说，为我们的罪死了，
verses.en: For I passed on to you as of first importance[NOTE:1] what I also received—that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures,
notes: Grk “among (the) first things.”

verses.zh: 而且埋葬了；又照圣经所说，第三天复活了，
verses.en: and that he was buried, and that he was raised[NOTE:1] on the third day according to the scriptures,
notes: Grk “he has been raised/is raised,” using a Greek tense that points to the present effect of the act of raising him. But in English idiom the temporal phrase “on the third day” requires a different translation of the verb.

verses.zh: 并且显给矶法看，然后显给十二使徒看；
verses.en: and that he appeared to Cephas,[NOTE:1] then to the twelve.
notes: Cephas. This individual is generally identified with the Apostle Peter (L&N 93.211). Both the Aramaic name “Cephas” and the Greek name “Peter” are related to words in each language which mean “rock.”

verses.zh: 后来一时显给五百多弟兄看，其中一大半到如今还在，却也有已经睡了的。
verses.en: Then he appeared to more than 500 of the brothers and sisters[NOTE:1] at one time, most of whom are still alive,[NOTE:2] though some have fallen asleep.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:10.
Grk “most of whom remain until now.”

The verb κοιμάω (koimaō) literally means “sleep,” but it is often used in the Bible as a euphemism for death when speaking of believers. This metaphorical usage by its very nature emphasizes the hope of resurrection: Believers will one day “wake up” out of death. Here the term refers to death, but “sleep” was used in the translation to emphasize the metaphorical, rhetorical usage of the term.

verses.zh: 以后显给雅各看，再显给众使徒看，
verses.en: Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles.

verses.zh: 末了也显给我看；我如同未到产期而生的人一般。
verses.en: Last of all, as though to one born at the wrong time,[NOTE:1] he appeared to me also.
notes: One born at the wrong time. The Greek word used here (ἔκτρωμα, ektrōma) refers to a premature birth, a miscarriage, or an aborted child. Paul uses it as a powerful figure of the unexpected, abnormal nature of his apostolic call.

verses.zh: 我原是使徒中最小的，不配称为使徒，因为我从前逼迫　神的教会。
verses.en: For I am the least of the apostles, unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

verses.zh: 然而，我今日成了何等人，是蒙　神的恩才成的，并且他所赐我的恩不是徒然的。我比众使徒格外劳苦；这原不是我，乃是　神的恩与我同在。
verses.en: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace to me has not been in vain. In fact, I worked harder than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God with me.

verses.zh: 不拘是我，是众使徒，我们如此传，你们也如此信了。
verses.en: Whether then it was I or they, this is the way we preach and this is the way you believed.

verses.zh: 既传基督是从死里复活了，怎么在你们中间有人说没有死人复活的事呢？
verses.en: Now if Christ is being preached as raised from the dead,[NOTE:1] how can some of you say there is no resurrection of the dead?
notes: Grk “that he has been raised from the dead.”

verses.zh: 若没有死人复活的事，基督也就没有复活了。
verses.en: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.

verses.zh: 若基督没有复活，我们所传的便是枉然，你们所信的也是枉然；
verses.en: And if Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is futile and your faith is empty.

verses.zh: 并且明显我们是为　神妄作见证的，因我们见证　神是叫基督复活了。若死人真不复活，　神也就没有叫基督复活了。
verses.en: Also, we are found to be false witnesses about God, because we have testified against God that he raised Christ from the dead, when in reality he did not raise him, if indeed the dead are not raised.

verses.zh: 因为死人若不复活，基督也就没有复活了。
verses.en: For if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised.

verses.zh: 基督若没有复活，你们的信便是徒然，你们仍在罪里。
verses.en: And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is useless; you are still in your sins.

verses.zh: 就是在基督里睡了的人也灭亡了。
verses.en: Furthermore, those who have fallen asleep[NOTE:1] in Christ have also perished.
notes: See the note on the word “asleep” in 15:6. This term is also used in v. 20.

verses.zh: 我们若靠基督只在今生有指望，就算比众人更可怜。
verses.en: For if only in this life we have hope in Christ, we should be pitied more than anyone.

verses.zh: 但基督已经从死里复活，成为睡了之人初熟的果子。
verses.en: But now Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.

verses.zh: 死既是因一人而来，死人复活也是因一人而来。
verses.en: For since death came through a man,[NOTE:1] the resurrection of the dead also came through a man.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “through a human being” (a reference to Adam).
Or “through a human being” (a reference to Jesus Christ).

verses.zh: 在亚当里众人都死了；照样，在基督里众人也都要复活。
verses.en: For just as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.

verses.zh: 但各人是按着自己的次序复活：初熟的果子是基督；以后，在他来的时候，是那些属基督的。
verses.en: But each in his own order: Christ, the firstfruits; then when Christ comes, those who belong to him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “then those who belong to Christ, at his coming.”

verses.zh: 再后，末期到了，那时基督既将一切执政的、掌权的、有能的都毁灭了，就把国交与父　神。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] comes the end,[NOTE:2] when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, when he has brought to an end all rule and all authority and power.
notes: This is a continuation of the previous sentence in the Greek text. Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Grk “then the end” or “then (is) the end.” Paul explains how the “end” relates to resurrection in vv. 25-28.

verses.zh: 因为基督必要作王，等　神把一切仇敌都放在他的脚下。
verses.en: For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.

verses.zh: 尽末了所毁灭的仇敌就是死。
verses.en: The last enemy to be eliminated is death.

verses.zh: 因为经上说：「　神叫万物都服在他的脚下。」既说万物都服了他，明显那叫万物服他的，不在其内了。
verses.en: For he has put everything in subjection under his feet.[NOTE:1] But when it says “everything” has been put in subjection, it is clear that this does not include the one who put everything in subjection to him.
notes: A quotation from Ps 8:6.

verses.zh: 万物既服了他，那时子也要自己服那叫万物服他的，叫　神在万物之上，为万物之主。
verses.en: And when all things are subjected to him, then the Son himself will be subjected to the one who subjected everything to him, so that God may be all in all.

gr.gloss: shall have been put in subjection

verses.zh: 不然，那些为死人受洗的，将来怎样呢？若死人总不复活，因何为他们受洗呢？
verses.en: Otherwise, what will those do who are baptized for the dead?[NOTE:1] If the dead are not raised at all, then why are they baptized for them?
notes: Many suggestions have been offered for the puzzling expression baptized for the dead. There are up to 200 different explanations for the passage; a summary is given by K. C. Thompson, “I Corinthians 15, 29 and Baptism for the Dead,” Studia Evangelica 2.1 (TU 87), 647-59. The most likely interpretation is that some Corinthians had undergone baptism to bear witness to the faith of fellow believers who had died without experiencing that rite themselves. Paul’s reference to the practice here is neither a recommendation nor a condemnation. He simply uses it as evidence from the lives of the Corinthians themselves to bolster his larger argument, begun in 15:12, that resurrection from the dead is a present reality in Christ and a future reality for them. Whatever they may have proclaimed, the Corinthians’ actions demonstrated that they had hope for a bodily resurrection.

verses.zh: 我们又因何时刻冒险呢？
verses.en: Why too are we in danger every hour?

verses.zh: 弟兄们，我在我主基督耶稣里，指着你们所夸的口极力地说，我是天天冒死。
verses.en: Every day I am in danger of death! This is as sure as[NOTE:1] my boasting in you,[NOTE:2] which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
notes: Or, more literally, “I swear by the boasting in you.”

‡ Although the witnesses for the shorter reading (P46 D F G Ψ 075 0243 1739 1881 M) are not as strong as for the addition of ἀδελφοί (adelphoi, “brothers”) at this juncture (א A B K P 33 81 104 365 1175 2464 lat sy co), it is difficult to find a reason why scribes would either intentionally or unintentionally drop the address here. Thus, the shorter reading is slightly preferred.

verses.zh: 我若当日像寻常人，在以弗所同野兽战斗，那于我有甚么益处呢？若死人不复活，我们就吃吃喝喝吧！因为明天要死了。
verses.en: If from a human point of view I fought with wild beasts at Ephesus,[NOTE:1] what did it benefit me? If the dead are not raised, let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see JP1-D2; JP2-D2; JP3-D2; JP4-D2.
An allusion to Isa 22:13; 56:12.

verses.zh: 你们不要自欺；滥交是败坏善行。
verses.en: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good morals.”[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from the poet Menander, Thais 218, which Paul uses in a proverbial sense.

verses.zh: 你们要醒悟为善，不要犯罪，因为有人不认识　神。我说这话是要叫你们羞愧。
verses.en: Sober up as you should, and stop sinning! For some have no knowledge of God—I say this to your shame!

verses.zh: 或有人问：「死人怎样复活，带着甚么身体来呢？」
verses.en: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised? With what kind of body will they come?”

verses.zh: 无知的人哪，你所种的，若不死就不能生。
verses.en: Fool! What you sow will not come to life unless it dies.

verses.zh: 并且你所种的不是那将来的形体，不过是子粒，即如麦子，或是别样的谷。
verses.en: And what you sow is not the body that is to be, but a bare seed[NOTE:1]—perhaps of wheat or something else.
notes: Grk “and what you sow, you do not sow the body that will be, but a bare seed.”

verses.zh: 但　神随自己的意思给他一个形体，并叫各等子粒各有自己的形体。
verses.en: But God gives it a body just as he planned, and to each of the seeds a body of its own.

verses.zh: 凡肉体各有不同：人是一样，兽又是一样，鸟又是一样，鱼又是一样。
verses.en: All flesh is not the same: People have one flesh, animals have another, birds and fish another.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “all flesh is not the same flesh, but there is one (flesh) of people, but another flesh of animals and another flesh of birds and another of fish.”

verses.zh: 有天上的形体，也有地上的形体；但天上形体的荣光是一样，地上形体的荣光又是一样。
verses.en: And there are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. The glory of the heavenly body is one sort and the earthly another.

verses.zh: 日有日的荣光，月有月的荣光，星有星的荣光；这星和那星的荣光也有分别。
verses.en: There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon and another glory of the stars, for star differs from star in glory.

verses.zh: 死人复活也是这样：所种的是必朽坏的，复活的是不朽坏的；
verses.en: It is the same with the resurrection of the dead. What is sown is perishable, what is raised is imperishable.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “it is sown in corruption, it is raised in incorruption.” The “it” refers to the body, as v. 44 shows.

verses.zh: 所种的是羞辱的，复活的是荣耀的；所种的是软弱的，复活的是强壮的；
verses.en: It is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory; it is sown in weakness, it is raised in power;

verses.zh: 所种的是血气的身体，复活的是灵性的身体。若有血气的身体，也必有灵性的身体。
verses.en: it is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.

verses.zh: 经上也是这样记着说：「首先的人亚当成了有灵（灵：或译血气）的活人」；末后的亚当成了叫人活的灵。
verses.en: So also it is written, “The first man, Adam, became a living person”;[NOTE:1] the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
notes: Grk “living soul”; a quotation from Gen 2:7.

verses.zh: 但属灵的不在先，属血气的在先，以后才有属灵的。
verses.en: However, the spiritual did not come first, but the natural, and then the spiritual.

verses.zh: 头一个人是出于地，乃属土；第二个人是出于天。
verses.en: The first man is from the earth, made of dust; the second man is from heaven.

verses.zh: 那属土的怎样，凡属土的也就怎样；属天的怎样，凡属天的也就怎样。
verses.en: Like the one made of dust, so too are those made of dust, and like the one from heaven, so too those who are heavenly.

verses.zh: 我们既有属土的形状，将来也必有属天的形状。
verses.en: And just as we have borne the image of the man of dust, let us also bear[NOTE:1] the image of the man of heaven.
notes: ‡ A few significant witnesses have the future indicative φορέσομεν (phoresomen, “we will bear”; B I 6 630 1881 al sa) instead of the aorist subjunctive φορέσωμεν (phoresōmen, “let us bear”; P46 א A C D F G Ψ 075 0243 33 1739 M latt bo). If the original reading is the future tense, then “we will bear” would be a guarantee that believers would be like Jesus (and unlike Adam) in the resurrection. If the aorist subjunctive is original, then “let us bear” would be a command to show forth the image of Jesus, i.e., to live as citizens of the kingdom that believers will one day inherit. The future indicative is not widespread geographically. At the same time, it fits the context well: Not only are there indicatives in this section (especially vv. 42-49), but the conjunction καί (kai) introducing the comparative καθώς (kathōs) seems best to connect to the preceding by furthering the same argument (what is, not what ought to be). For this reason, though, the future indicative could be a reading thus motivated by an early scribe. In light of the extremely weighty evidence for the aorist subjunctive, it is probably best to regard the aorist subjunctive as autographic. This connects well with v. 50, for there Paul makes a pronouncement that seems to presuppose some sort of exhortation. G. D. Fee (First Corinthians [NICNT], 795) argues for the originality of the subjunctive, stating that “it is nearly impossible to account for anyone’s having changed a clearly understandable future to the hortatory subjunctive so early and so often that it made its way into every textual history as the predominant reading.” The subjunctive makes a great deal of sense in view of the occasion of 1 Corinthians. Paul wrote to combat an over-realized eschatology in which some of the Corinthians evidently believed they were experiencing all the benefits of the resurrection body in the present, and thus that their behavior did not matter. If the subjunctive is the correct reading, it seems Paul makes two points: (1) that the resurrection is a bodily one, as distinct from an out-of-body experience, and (2) that one’s behavior in the interim does make a difference (see 15:32-34, 58).

verses.zh: 弟兄们，我告诉你们说，血肉之体不能承受　神的国，必朽坏的不能承受不朽坏的。
verses.en: Now this is what I am saying, brothers and sisters:[NOTE:1] Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:10.

verses.zh: 我如今把一件奥秘的事告诉你们：我们不是都要睡觉，乃是都要改变，
verses.en: Listen,[NOTE:1] I will tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep,[NOTE:2] but we will all be changed—
notes: Grk “Behold.”

See the note on the word “asleep” in 15:6.tc The manuscripts are grouped into four basic readings here: (1) א C 0243* 33 1739 have “we all will sleep, but we will not all be changed” (πάντες κοιμηθησόμεθα, οὐ πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα); (2) P46 Ac (F G) have “we will not all sleep, but we will not all be changed” (πάντες οὐ κοιμηθησόμεθα, οὐ πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα); (3) D* lat Tert Ambst Spec read “we will all rise, but we will not all be changed.” (4) The wording πάντες οὐ κοιμηθησόμεθα, πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα (“we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed”) is found in B D2 Ψ 075 0243c 1881 M sy co. How shall we interpret such data? In light of the fact that Paul and his generation did in fact die, early scribes may have felt some embarrassment over the bald statement, “We will not all sleep” (πάντες οὐ κοιμηθησόμεθα). This could account for the first variant. Although the second variant could be viewed as a conflation of (1) and (4) (so TCGNT 502; G. D. Fee, First Corinthians [NICNT], 796), it could also have arisen consciously, to guard against the notion that all whom Paul was addressing should regard themselves as true believers. The third variant, prominent in the Western witnesses, may have arisen to counter those who would deny the final resurrection (so TCGNT 502). In any event, since the fourth reading has the best credentials externally and best explains the rise of the others it should be adopted as the authentic wording here.

verses.zh: 就在一霎时，眨眼之间，号筒末次吹响的时候。因号筒要响，死人要复活成为不朽坏的，我们也要改变。
verses.en: in a moment, in the blinking[NOTE:1] of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
notes: The Greek word ῥιπή (rhipē) refers to a very rapid movement (BDAG 906 s.v.). This has traditionally been translated as “twinkling,” which implies an exceedingly fast—almost instantaneous—movement of the eyes, but this could be confusing to the modern reader since twinkling in modern English often suggests a faint, flashing light. In conjunction with the genitive ὀφθαλμοῦ (ophthalmou, “of an eye”), “blinking” is the best English equivalent (see, e.g., L&N 16.5), although it does not convey the exact speed implicit in the Greek term.

verses.zh: 这必朽坏的总要变成（变成：原文是穿；下同）不朽坏的，这必死的总要变成不死的。
verses.en: For this perishable body must put on the imperishable, and this mortal body must put on immortality.

verses.zh: 这必朽坏的既变成不朽坏的，这必死的既变成不死的，那时经上所记「死被得胜吞灭」的话就应验了。
verses.en: Now when this perishable puts on the imperishable, and this mortal puts on immortality, then the saying that is written will happen,“Death has been swallowed up in victory.”[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Isa 25:8.

verses.zh: 死啊！你得胜的权势在哪里？死啊！你的毒钩在哪里？
verses.en: “Where, O death, is your victory?Where, O death, is your sting?”[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Hos 13:14.

verses.zh: 死的毒钩就是罪，罪的权势就是律法。
verses.en: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.

verses.zh: 感谢　神，使我们藉着我们的主耶稣基督得胜。
verses.en: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!

verses.zh: 所以，我亲爱的弟兄们，你们务要坚固，不可摇动，常常竭力多做主工；因为知道，你们的劳苦在主里面不是徒然的。
verses.en: So then, dear brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] be firm. Do not be moved! Always be outstanding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:10.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- It is obvious from the context that Paul is reacting to a local potential heresy that denied the resurrection of the dead.
This could be another question from the church or information from visitors from the church. Several theories have been
postulated as to the possible origin:

- incipient Gnostic (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GNOSTICISM) ideas which emphasized the dualism between spirit (i.e., God,
which is good) and matter (i.e., material things, which are evil)

- those asserting that the resurrection has already occurred (cf. 2 Tim. 2:17-18), but only affected Jesus.

- This chapter is the definitive passage in the NT on

- the resurrection of Christ

- the resurrection of believers

It must be remembered that this passage was probably written before any of the Gospels were written down. Note
the Special Topic and the related sermon in the Special Topic Index.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RESURRECTION

- Notice Paul's pastoral emphasis in the way this doctrinal chapter ends, 1 Cor. 15:58. This is similar to 1 Thess. 4:18.
Paul always brings doctrine down to daily living and serving. Truth must inform and transform lifestyle! Truth is, in reality, a person (cf.
John 8:32; 14:6; 1 John 5:20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRUTH/TRUE

"With Mark probably being the first written Gospel, this is the first use of the term

(i.e., FUTURE ACTIVE INDICATIVE). Both of these Greek words were pronounced similarly. The early
manuscripts were often copied at one time by one man reading the text aloud and several men making written copies.
Theologically the FUTURE INDICATIVE is preferable. The other VERBS in context are
FUTURE. It is a descriptive context, not hortatory (i.e., exhortation to action).

15:51 "mystery" God has a unified purpose for mankind's redemption that even precedes the Fall (Genesis 3).
Hints of this plan are revealed in the OT (Genesis 3:15; 12:3; Exodus 19:5-6; and the universal passages in
the prophets). However, this inclusive agenda was not clear (1 Cor. 2:6-8; Eph. 2:11-3:13). With the coming of Jesus and the
Spirit it begins to become more obvious. Paul used the term "mystery" to describe this total redemptive plan,
which was once hidden, but now fully revealed (1 Cor. 4:1; Eph. 3:3-11; 6:19; Col. 4:3; 1 Tim. 1:9). However, he used
it in several different senses.

- A partial hardening of Israel to allow Gentiles to be included. This influx of Gentiles will work
as a mechanism (jealousy) for Jews to accept Jesus as the Messiah of prophecy (Rom. 11:25-32).

- The gospel was made known to the nations, all of whom are potentially included in Christ and
through Christ (Rom. 16:25-27; Col. 2:2).

- Believers will have new bodies at the Second Coming (1 Cor. 15:51-57; 1 Thess. 4:13-18).

- The summing up of all things in Christ (Eph. 1:8-11).

- The Gentiles and Jews are fellow-heirs (Eph. 2:11-3:13).

- Intimacy of the relationship between Christ and the Church described in marriage terms (Eph. 5:22-33).

- Gentiles included in the covenant people and indwelt by the Spirit of Christ so as to produce Christlike
maturity, that is, the restored image of God in fallen humanity (Gen. 1:26-27; 5:1; Col. 1:26-28).

- The end-time AntiChrist (2 Thess. 2:1-11).

- An early church summary of the mystery is found in 1 Tim. 3:16.
